newsitem.title: POLAND: Dragon, not Big Bird, welcomes Poland to Sesame St.
newsitem.headline: Dragon, not Big Bird, welcomes Poland to Sesame St.

text.p: A large friendly dragon rather than Big Bird will welcome Polish children to their country's version of the U.S. television show Sesame Street, which begins showing here on October 27.
The show's producers said on Monday that the Polish version aimed at all children and their parents, could particularly help children in the countryside and small towns learn to read.
"The difference between the quality of education between Warsaw and small towns can be quite large," Maciej Kosinski, the show's artistic producer, told Reuters.

Sesame Street is shown in about 140 countries around the world though Poland is the first former-communist Central European country to produce its own version rather than merely dubbing versions of the original.

Kosinski's Euromedia TV has produced a year's worth of episodes to be shown on Polish television's channel 2, which received a licence from the Children's Television Workshop that created the original Sesame Street in 1969.

The Polish version, which for the Polish audience takes place in a courtyard between blocks of flats rather than on a street, also features a second muppet, little lamb Beata, and humans including a Lech-Walesa-looking grandfather figure.

Traditional Sesame Street favourites such as Ernie and Bert will make occasional cameo appearances under Polish names while Big Bird will be known to the Polish audience of nearly 40 million as Zoltodziob, or yellow beak.
